question.text: How many vehicles will the Texas DMV automated-vehicle registry have listed for Tesla on December 29, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the number of VINs listed at the [Tesla Robotaxi, LLC](https://txmccs.txdmv.gov/truckstop/companies/81edcff1-8a6e-4ed0-be1f-60668515e223/automated-motor-vehicles) at the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) automated motor vehicle database, when accessed by Metaculus on or after December 29, 2026.
question.fine_print: If the resolution source is unavailable, the question may resolve according to  [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).

# Tesla Robotaxi, LLC on the Texas DMV automated-vehicle registry: research notes (as of 2026-11-10)

The latest count I found is about 1,282 vehicles, from roughly Nov 8-9 (tracker-reported). I couldn't confirm it on the DMV page itself.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-10: I fetched the TxMCCS page for Tesla Robotaxi, LLC, but only the title "TxMCCS - Texas Motor Carrier Credentialing System" came back, with no VINs. The list is probably loaded by JavaScript, so I couldn't read the count directly. [TxDMV](https://txmccs.txdmv.gov/truckstop/companies/81edcff1-8a6e-4ed0-be1f-60668515e223/automated-motor-vehicles)
- Around 2026-11-08/09: The latest reported count is 1,282, after 38 Model Ys were added to the previous 1,244. Waymo is at 1,285. The source is the robotaxitracker.com Texas tracker, reported by @pbeisel and Drive Tesla. I worked out the date from the X post ID: it is about 12 days after the Oct 27 post. [X](https://x.com/pbeisel/status/2119607693145264342), [Drive Tesla](https://driveteslacanada.ca/news/tesla-robotaxi-texas-registry-1282-closes-in-on-waymo/)
- The registry lists only VIN, model year, make and model. It shows which vehicles are authorized, not which are in service. [TeslaNorth](https://teslanorth.com/2026/10/09/texas-cybercab-registry/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. The count, about 1,282, sits just above the bottom of the question's range (1,200 to 4,200), and there are about 49 days left.
- Every reported update has been an increase. I found no reports of vehicles being removed, but I couldn't check whether removals can happen.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-09: Tesla started Robotaxi service in San Antonio, its fourth Texas city after Austin, Dallas and Houston, and expanded the Austin service area. Fleet size wasn't disclosed. [Drive Tesla](https://driveteslacanada.ca/news/tesla-robotaxi-san-antonio-launch-austin-expansion/), [Diario Bitcoin](https://www.diariobitcoin.com/estados-unidos/tesla-lleva-sus-robotaxis-a-san-antonio-y-amplia-su-pulso-con-waymo/)
- 2026-11-06: Musk said Cybertruck production at Giga Texas will wind down by mid-2027 to free capacity for Cybercab. [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/tech/tesla-plans-wind-down-cybertruck-production-after-sales-slump)
- Early Nov 2026: Benzinga reported 1,244 Tesla vs 1,259 Waymo, a 128% rise in just over a month. [Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/trading-ideas/long-ideas/26/11/62781991/tesla-robotaxi-waymo-texas)
- 2026-10-31/11-01: 1,204 vehicles (631 Model Y, 573 Cybercab), after 124 Model Ys were added. [TeslaNorth](https://teslanorth.com/2026/11/01/texas-robotaxi-fleet-1204/)
- 2026-10-21: On the Q3 earnings call, Tesla said Cybercab would come to Dallas "next month", it is trying to deliver Cybercabs to customers by the end of 2026, and so far every Cybercab built has gone to its own fleet. It gave no weekly output figure and no year-end fleet target. [TeslaNorth](https://teslanorth.com/2026/10/21/tesla-q3-2026-call-takeaways/)

## 4. Base rates and trend
Reported registry counts (from tracker snapshots and articles):
- 2026-05-28: 42 (Waymo 577). [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/28/tesla-robotaxi-fleet-texas-one-tenth-size-of-waymos-filings-reveal.html)
- 2026-08-31: about 314 (269 Model Y, 45 Cybercab). [TeslaNorth](https://teslanorth.com/2026/09/02/tesla-robotaxi-texas-420/)
- 2026-09-03: 420 (375 Model Y, 45 Cybercab). Same source.
- Around 2026-09-26: about 546 (420 + 126). [Tesla Oracle](https://www.teslaoracle.com/2026/09/26/tesla-robotaxi-and-cybercab-fleet-in-texas-surpasses-the-500-mark-420-126/)
- Early Oct: 589. Then by about 2026-10-09: 739 (420 Model Y, 319 Cybercab). [TeslaNorth](https://teslanorth.com/2026/10/09/texas-cybercab-registry/)
- Late Oct: 970, then 1,051 on 10-27 (544 Cybercab, 507 Model Y). [TeslaNorth](https://teslanorth.com/2026/10/27/tesla-cybercab-outnumbers-model-y-texas/), [X](https://x.com/RtaxiTracker/status/2115139092828602378)
- 2026-10-28: 1,080 (+29 Cybercab). [BASENOR](https://www.basenor.com/blogs/news/tesla-robotaxi-fleet-tops-1-000-in-texas-as-cybercab-passes-model-y)
- 2026-11-01: 1,204. Early Nov: 1,244. Around 11-08/09: 1,282.

What the trend looks like:
- Vehicles are added in batches of 29 to 150 every few days.
- Average pace: about 13 a day from Sep 3 to Nov 9, about 17 to 18 a day from Oct 9 to Nov 9, and about 10 a day from Nov 1 to Nov 9 (a slowdown).
- Simply carrying those paces forward 49 days would add about 500 to 850 vehicles. That is arithmetic, not a forecast.
- Seasonality: the registry only started in May 2026, so there are no earlier years to compare. I don't know whether holidays slow down registrations.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no market on this registry count on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold.
- Related markets:
  - Kalshi, "Which states will robotaxi be offered to this year?": Florida 0.90, Nevada 0.62, Arizona 0.47.
  - Polymarket, Tesla robotaxi launch in California by Dec 31: 7%. Polymarket, Q4 deliveries: the 450k to 475k bucket is the most likely at 0.275.
  - Manifold: 79% that the Cybercab gives public rides in Dallas by Nov 30, 2026. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/BarryJones/will-teslas-steeringwheelless-cyber)
- Only the Manifold Dallas Cybercab market bears on Texas fleet growth, and only indirectly.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- November 2026: Cybercab launch in Dallas, which would probably mean registering more Cybercabs. San Antonio is also ramping up after its Nov 9 launch.
- Cybercab production: Musk said the ramp would accelerate "exponentially" toward the end of the year, and every unit so far has gone to Tesla's own fleet. Cybercabs delivered to customers may not show up under the Robotaxi LLC listing. I couldn't confirm either way. [Not a Tesla App](https://notateslaapp.com/news/4867/tesla-q3-2026-earnings-call-recap-everything-you-need-to-know)
- Late Dec 2026: the end-of-quarter delivery push and holidays could change how often batches appear.
- NHTSA is auditing Cybercab safety certification (it estimated about 1,000 affected vehicles, with Tesla's answers due Oct 30). I found no outcome yet. [TeslaNorth](https://teslanorth.com/2026/10/09/texas-cybercab-registry/)
- Weather doesn't apply here.

Sources: the links given inline above.

## Research summary: Tesla VINs on the Texas DMV automated-vehicle registry

**Short version:** The best current count is **1,282 Tesla VINs as of Nov 9, 2026**, from a third-party scraper that I could not check against the official page. Nothing so far settles the question. The count has grown about 3x since mid-September, but it has come in irregular batches and slowed sharply in November. December 29 is 50 days from Nov 9.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-10: I fetched the TxDMV Tesla Robotaxi, LLC page directly, but it only returned the page title ("TxMCCS"). It needs JavaScript to load, so I could not confirm a count from it myself. [TxDMV](https://txmccs.txdmv.gov/truckstop/companies/81edcff1-8a6e-4ed0-be1f-60668515e223/automated-motor-vehicles)
- 2026-11-09 18:08 UTC: A GitHub tracker that scrapes the TxDMV list shows Tesla Robotaxi, LLC (authorization AV8313426653583, status "authorized") with **1,282 vehicles**. Since Nov 5 it no longer splits Model Y from Cybercab: one batch of entries spells the model "Modey Y" and the newest entries have no model at all. The total still looks reliable. [tracker status.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/derekbeau1/tx-robotaxi-tracker/main/data/status.json)
- 2026-11-10: A second tracker shows 1,244 for Tesla, but it gives no date, so it is probably an older snapshot. [platformaeronaut](https://avrideshare.platformaeronaut.com/tracker/texas/operators/tesla-robotaxi)

### 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the outcome yet. The count needs about 50 days of change from 1,282, which is already near the bottom of the question's 1,200 to 4,200 range.
- The list can shrink as well as grow: on Nov 1 the tracker logged 2 entries removed and 1 re-added. [tracker](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/derekbeau1/tx-robotaxi-tracker/main/data/status.json)

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-09: Robotaxi service launched in San Antonio; Fort Worth was also added in November. [diariobitcoin](https://www.diariobitcoin.com/estados-unidos/tesla-lleva-sus-robotaxis-a-san-antonio-y-amplia-su-pulso-con-waymo/), [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_Robotaxi)
- 2026-11-09: The tracker logged 38 new Tesla VINs with no model listed, bringing the total from 1,244 to 1,282. [GitHub issue #7](https://github.com/derekbeau1/tx-robotaxi-tracker/issues/7)
- 2026-11-06: Musk said Cybertruck production will wind down by mid-2027 to free up capacity for the Cybercab. [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/tech/tesla-plans-wind-down-cybertruck-production-after-sales-slump)
- 2026-11-01: Tesla stood at 1,204 (631 Model Y, 573 Cybercab), compared with Waymo at 1,259. [TeslaNorth](https://teslanorth.com/2026/11/01/texas-robotaxi-fleet-1204/)
- 2026-10-22: On the Q3 earnings call, Tesla cited more than 125,000 units of installed Cybercab capacity but gave no weekly production figure. Executive Lars Moravy said output is matched to the needs of Tesla's own robotaxi fleet and that customer deliveries are planned by the end of 2026. Dallas was named as the next Cybercab city. [TeslaNorth](https://teslanorth.com/2026/10/21/tesla-q3-2026-call-takeaways/), [Fool transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/10/22/tesla-tsla-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)
- 2026-09-22: Only about 265 of 476 registered VINs had been matched to plates seen on the road, and 8 were seen carrying riders in the prior week. Registered numbers are far above active vehicles. [Electrek](https://electrek.co/2026/09/22/tesla-robotaxi-active-fleet-austin-crashes-8-vehicles/)

### 4. Base rates and trend
The series only started on 2026-05-28, so there are no earlier years to compare and no seasonal pattern to check.

Tesla count history:
- 2026-05-28: 42, the first count when TxDMV disclosure began. [evxl](https://evxl.co/2026/05/31/tesla-robotaxi-fleet-filings-42-texas-vehicles/)
- ~2026-09-03: about 420, including about 45 Cybercabs. Cybercabs first appeared on Aug 31. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_Robotaxi), [evwire](https://evwire.com/p/tesla-cybercab-texas-registrations-349)
- 2026-09-22: 476. [Electrek](https://electrek.co/2026/09/22/tesla-robotaxi-active-fleet-austin-crashes-8-vehicles/)
- 2026-10-15: 769 (349 Cybercab, 420 Model Y). [evwire](https://evwire.com/p/tesla-cybercab-texas-registrations-349)
- 2026-10-21: 811 (449 Cybercab, 362 Model Y, as reported by CNBC). These two splits are inconsistent: Model Y would have dropped from 420 to 362 in six days with no explanation. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_Robotaxi)
- 2026-10-24: 970; 10-27: 1,051; 10-28: 1,080; 10-31: 1,204; 11-01: 1,244; 11-09: 1,282. [tracker](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/derekbeau1/tx-robotaxi-tracker/main/data/status.json), [TeslaNorth](https://teslanorth.com/2026/10/27/tesla-cybercab-outnumbers-model-y-texas/)

Growth rates over different windows:
- Sep 22 to Nov 9: about 17 per day.
- Oct 15 to Nov 9: about 20 per day.
- Oct 24 to Nov 1: about 34 per day, the peak.
- Nov 1 to Nov 9: about 5 per day.

Additions come in batches of 30 to 150, with quiet stretches between them; the Model Y count sat at 420 for weeks at a time. If any of those rates held for the 50 days to Dec 29, the total would land somewhere between roughly 1,500 and 2,300. The fastest rates would push it higher. These are arithmetic projections only, not a forecast.

### 5. Other forecasts
- I found no market or expert forecast on the registry count itself.
- Related Kalshi markets (as of Nov 10):
  - Robotaxi offered in Florida in 2026: 90%; Nevada: 62%; Arizona: 47%.
  - Tesla 2026 production above 1.8M: 81%.
- Polymarket: robotaxis in California by Dec 31: about 7%.
- Manifold: steering-wheel-less Cybercab giving public rides in Dallas by Nov 30: 79%. A Dallas launch would likely bring more Cybercab registrations. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/BarryJones/will-teslas-steeringwheelless-cyber)

### 6. Upcoming events before Dec 29
- A Cybercab launch in Dallas and Fort Worth was guided for after Q3 and is expected around November. [TeslaNorth](https://teslanorth.com/2026/10/21/tesla-q3-2026-call-takeaways/)
- The San Antonio fleet build-out after the Nov 9 launch could add Model Y or Cybercab registrations.
- Planned Cybercab customer deliveries by end of 2026: it is unclear whether privately owned cars would appear under Tesla Robotaxi, LLC's authorization.
- Tesla's Q4 production push and the planned Cybertruck-to-Cybercab line conversion.
- A data risk: TxDMV entries now have missing or misspelled model fields, so the model breakdowns may stay unreliable. The total VIN count is what resolves the question.
- Weather is not a material factor.

(b) Latest known value: about 1,282 vehicles around Nov 8-9, 2026. This comes from tracker reports (robotaxitracker.com, via @pbeisel and Drive Tesla). It was not confirmed on the DMV page itself, which loads its list with JavaScript.

(c) If nothing changed: about 1,282.

(d) If the current trend continued:
- At the recent slower pace of about 10 a day: about 1,770.
- At the Oct 9 to Nov 9 pace of 17-18 a day: about 2,150.
- At the Sep 3 to Nov 9 average of about 13 a day: about 1,920.

(e) Historical variation:
- Over the past 49 days (about Sep 21 to Nov 9), the count rose from roughly 500 to 1,282, a gain of about 750.
- Additions come in lumpy batches of 29 to 150 every few days.
- Growth has been strongly positive, but the pace varies by a factor of two or more between months.

(f) Expert and market expectations:
- There is no market on this count.
- Tesla says the Cybercab ramp will accelerate toward year-end and that Cybercab is launching in Dallas in November.
- Service launched in San Antonio on Nov 9.
- All of these point to continued registrations, possibly faster ones.
- Pulling the other way: Cybercabs delivered to customers may not appear under Robotaxi LLC, and holidays could slow batches.

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
- Low: NHTSA's certification audit, a safety incident or a regulatory pause halts new Cybercab registrations, and Model Y additions stall over the holidays. The count could end near 1,300-1,400, or even dip if vehicles are removed.
- High: the Cybercab ramp truly goes "exponential," with hundreds a week registered for the Dallas, Houston and San Antonio expansions plus large Model Y batches. That could push the count above 3,000.

- Percentile 99 reflects a dramatic Cybercab production surge that sends nearly all output to the Texas fleet.
